liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Thunderous rendition of the song; Jam sequence includes Drums, Me & My Uncle, and back to The Other One [10][16]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Sequence with Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad is energetic; Best Not Fade Away into Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad sequence [10][18]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' as an opening number is loved by the listener [20]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Beautiful performance featuring some interesting alternate lyrics [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-11-07.127503.fm.boswell.smith.flac16** (recommended): FM broadcast; 36 songs; 207 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1971-11-07.167790.FM.Menke-Miller.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 233 min [3]. Said about its sound: Monitor issues occurred throughout the first set [3]
- **gd71-11-07.prefm.kaplan.9570.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 31 songs; 214 min; rated 4.5/5 by 42 [5]. Said about its sound: Pre-FM reels have dropouts in Brown Eyed Woman and distorted piano; Sound quality leaves something to be desired compared to other archive shows; Piano feed distortion is a flaw in the recording [12][13][14][16][17][18][21]
- **gd1971-11-07.155687.remastered.boswell.smith.miller.flac24**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 220 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [7]
- **gd1971-11-07.169935.prefm.gdh.miller.flac1644**: pre-FM broadcast master; 31 songs; 194 min [9]. Said about its sound: Monitor issues occurred throughout the first set [9]

## Around the show

- First live Dead show acquired by the listener in the late 70s [11]
- Harding Theater feels like a living room with cool lights and comfy chairs [14]
- Show has a small, intimate, warm, and personal feeling [14]
- Band delivers with lots of energy and passion [17]
- Band seems to be having fun with laid back stage banter [21]
- New Riders Of The Purple Sage opened the show [3]
- New Riders Of The Purple Sage opened the show [9]
- Old 2nd gen cassette FM broadcast sounds better than these Pre-FM reels [12]
- 11/6/71 sounds better with more solid bass and less piano rattle [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-11-07.127503.fm.boswell.smith.flac16**: taped by Peter Kafer; transferred by Will Boswell; Matt Smith; source: FM MR @ 3/ 3.4 ips(Peter Kafer?)>R @ 3 & 3/4 ips(Will Boswell) [1]
- **gd1971-11-07.167790.FM.Menke-Miller.flac1648**: taped by Recording and Transfer by Bob Menke; transferred by Mastering by Charlie Miller  June 11, 2024; source: FM (KSFX-FM) > Master Reels (3.75ips 1/4trk) [3]
- **gd71-11-07.prefm.kaplan.9570.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Source is Pre-FM Reel transferred to DAT then CD via Seth Kaplan [5]
- **gd1971-11-07.155687.remastered.boswell.smith.miller.flac24**: taped by Tape supplied by Will Boswell; transferred by Transfer by Matt Smith Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 12, 2022; source: FM > Master Reel (3.75ips) > Reel (3.75ips) [7]. Also: Remastered version of shnid=127490 with 17 minutes of tunings patched from shnid=2580; Thanks to Matt Smith for allowing work on his source [7]
- **gd1971-11-07.169935.prefm.gdh.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 26, 2024; source: Pre-FM > Master Reels > DAT (44.1k) [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead: “Harding Theater 1971” (2016) CD Review](https://michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com/2017/09/grateful-dead-harding-theater-1971-2016.html) [23]
